title: Assembling, powering up and setting up a computer from scratch

videos.script: Everything in the first five lessons, put together with your own hands. {{hands}} Building a computer is not difficult and it is not delicate. Every connector goes in one way, nothing needs force, and the single most common mistake is a cable that is not quite in. What makes people nervous is that the first press of the power button is the whole test at once: it either draws a picture or it does not, and a blank screen says nothing about which of nine things is wrong. {{blank}} So this lesson is mostly about order. Do it in the order that lets each step be checked, test it outside the case before you tidy anything, and the blank screen becomes a list you work down rather than a wall. {{order}} We also do the two settings in the firmware that are worth changing and the dozen that are not, and the first day of a new installation, which is where a machine either gets a habit of being backed up or never does. {{after}} And we finish on a picture of a motherboard with the names taken off.
